proposed_comments.title: Match both canonical DOS paths and fallback kernel names in find_processes_recursive
proposed_comments.body:
### Match both canonical DOS paths and fallback kernel names in find_processes_recursive

**Severity:** high

The path map currently records only the canonical DOS/UNC value from `path_to_canonical_name`, but a handle can still fall back to the `\Device\...` kernel form when `GetFinalPathNameByHandleW` is unavailable or fails. In `find_processes_recursive`, the `kernel_paths_contain` check compares the handle name against only the canonical-form keys, so the fallback kernel path never matches and the process is silently missed. Keep the canonical entry and also register the fallback kernel name for each searched file and directory so both result paths resolve to the same process set.

proposed_comments.title: Preserve kernel path compatibility and add regression coverage for canonical + device-name resolution
proposed_comments.body:
### Preserve kernel path compatibility and add regression coverage for canonical + device-name resolution

**Severity:** medium

**Affected code:** `src/modules/FileLocksmith/FileLocksmithLibInterop/NtdllExtensions.h`, `src/modules/FileLocksmith/FileLocksmithLibInterop/NtdllExtensions.cpp`, and `src/modules/FileLocksmith/FileLocksmithCLI/tests/FileLocksmithCLITests.cpp`.

**Problem:** The PR description calls out compatibility for `HandleInfo::kernel_file_name` and `path_to_kernel_name`, but the current head renames them to `file_path` and `path_to_canonical_name` without retaining the compatibility surface. The same gap leaves the canonical and NT device-path behavior untested for the regression path that matters in CLI and handle resolution.

**Why it matters:** Consumer code and UI layers that still rely on the kernel-name names can stop compiling or fail to detect the right handle when a file opened by a device path falls back to `\Device\...` instead of the canonical DOS path.

**Suggested change:**
1. In `NtdllExtensions.h`, reintroduce `HandleInfo::kernel_file_name` and `path_to_kernel_name` as compatibility members/wrappers, while keeping the new canonical `file_path` and `path_to_canonical_name` helpers as the primary implementation.
2. In `NtdllExtensions.cpp`, keep the canonical conversion and copy the canonical result into `kernel_file_name` for the legacy field, or implement a thin wrapper that preserves the original NT-device `\Device\...` behavior without removing the new helper.
3. In `FileLocksmithCLITests.cpp`, add `TestCanonicalAndKernelPathHelpers` and assert both `path_to_canonical_name` and `path_to_kernel_name` on a temp file so the DOS/UNC value stays canonical while the fallback kernel value remains `\Device\...`-formatted.

```cpp
std::wstring path_to_kernel_name(LPCWSTR path) {
    return path_to_canonical_name(path); // legacy wrapper kept for compatibility
}
```

**Verification:** Rebuild the exact upstream head, run the File Locksmith CLI unit tests, and confirm the canonical and fallback-kernel cases are both covered by `TestCanonicalAndKernelPathHelpers` without regressing the existing output formatting checks.
